title: Minimal VDOM Diff & Patch Engine
subtopicTitle: Critical Rendering Path: Reflow vs Repaint
concept: Virtual DOM Reconciliation & Minimal Mutation Operations
problemStatement: Implement `diff(oldVNode, newVNode)` that returns a list of patch instructions (`{ type: 'REPLACE'|'TEXT'|'PROPS', ... }`) to update `oldVNode` into `newVNode` with minimal operations.
interviewTrap: Assuming that tag changes can be patched in place. If tags differ (`div` -> `span`), the entire node must be replaced.

testCases.name: Generates REPLACE patch when tag changes
testCases.testFn: const p = diff({ tag: 'div', props: {} }, { tag: 'span', props: {} }); return p[0].type;

testCases.name: Generates PROPS patch when attributes change
testCases.testFn: const p = diff({ tag: 'div', props: { className: 'old' } }, { tag: 'div', props: { className: 'active' } }); return p[0].props;

testCases.name: Returns empty patches when nodes are identical
testCases.testFn: const p = diff({ tag: 'div', props: { id: 'x' } }, { tag: 'div', props: { id: 'x' } }); return p.length;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Reflow recalculates geometry and layout tree (expensive). Repaint redraws pixels without changing geometry. Composite occurs on the GPU (transforms and opacity). Reading layout properties (`offsetWidth`, `scrollTop`) right after writing them forces synchronous layout thrashing.

2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Virtual DOM Reconciliation & Minimal Mutation Operations is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does React achieve O(N) tree diffing when the general tree edit distance problem is O(N^3)?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: General tree diffing (Levenshtein edit distance for trees) is O(N^3). React and modern VDOM engines achieve O(N) linear time using two heuristic assumptions: 1) Two elements of different types will produce different trees (replaces old tree entirely). 2) The developer can hint which child elements remain stable across renders using the `key` prop.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: The classic algorithmic computer science question in frontend interviews.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why should you NEVER use array index as a key in dynamic lists?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Using index keys (`key={index}`) breaks identity when items are prepended, deleted, or reordered. React matches the old index 0 fiber to the new index 0 item, preserving the old component's internal state (uncontrolled input text, animations) on the WRONG item.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: High-frequency bug source in production React apps.

realWorldUseCases.description: Diffing lists using key-based Map lookups to emit minimal DOM insertion, deletion, and relocation operations.

howToExplain.opening: A VDOM diff engine solves the tree reconciliation problem in linear O(N) time using heuristic type-checking and key-based child mapping.
keyPoints: O(N^3) general diff is reduced to O(N) via type comparison and keys.
Different element types unmount and recreate the subtree completely.
Same element types patch changed props and diff children.
Keys allow identifying reordered nodes without recreating DOM elements.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Reconciliation minimizes physical DOM mutations, which are the slowest part of browser rendering.
analogies: Moving house: if you label your moving boxes (keys), the movers put each box directly in the right room instead of unpacking everything into the living room and guessing.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming diffing modifies the real DOM immediately during tree traversal.
commonMistakes.why: Diffing accumulates a list of patches (Render Phase); mutations are applied in a single synchronous commit batch (Commit Phase).
commonMistakes.correct: Explain the separation between diffing (Render phase) and mutation (Commit phase).

followUpDeepDive.question: How does Preact's diffing algorithm differ from React Fiber?
followUpDeepDive.answer: Preact diffs directly against the live real DOM tree without an intermediate Fiber linked list, making it ~3KB in size compared to React's ~40KB Fiber reconciler.
